abstract: Aberrant events during mRNA translation trigger ribosome-dependent quality control mechanisms that tune mRNA decay and gene expression. Here, we describe endonucleolytic mRNA decay associated with damaged tRNAs at the ribosome. We provide evidence that this process is associated with a nicked tRNA that our data place in the ribosomal A-site, where it contributes to ribosome stalling. Genetic analyses suggest that the pathway is independent of canonical mRNA decay machinery, and we identify the carboxy-terminal domain kinase I (CTDK-I) complex as a critical regulator. These findings suggest that the ribosomal A-site can engage damaged tRNAs and that this engagement can trigger mRNA decay, broadening our understanding of translation elongation and tRNA biology.
